notes: Derived edit. died_in carries chain:located_in->died_in, so dying on Saint Helena, in the South Atlantic, south of the equator, is dying in the Southern Hemisphere; a firm rule turns death in a hemisphere into died_in_hemisphere (functional). The South Atlantic's definition (P3) is firm. q1 ('the same hemisphere as Paris') is a join through the functional died_in_hemisphere; Paris in the Northern Hemisphere, and in no other, is its bridge (firm, a class axiom with a nominal: located_in is transitive, so not functional). Relabelled dl on 2026-10-31 (COVERAGE.md label corrections); the fol section keeps its Z3 encoding as a second check.

queries.ask: napoleon : died_in_hemisphere some (Hemisphere and inv(located_in) value paris)

fol.notes: Places are an enumeration; the hemisphere of a place (in_hemisphere) and of Napoleon's death (died_in_hemisphere, functional) are uninterpreted functions to the two hemispheres, so the edit and the worlds can move them. The South Atlantic's definition (P3) and the rule from place of death to hemisphere of death are firm, as in the DL file. w2 moves Saint Helena north (its side fact).

local.in_hemisphere: in_hemisphere(x): the hemisphere (north or south of the equator) place x lies in; the functional value form of located_in to a hemisphere.
